claims.text: Baseline TiVNbTa is a single-phase BCC dendritic alloy.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa and compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa exhibits approximately 40% strain-to-failure at room temperature.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 5 at% W to TiVNbTa.
Added W atoms will remain in solid solution in the BCC TiVNbTa lattice.
W solutes will produce local lattice distortions in TiVNbTa.
W-induced lattice distortion will provide solid-solution strengthening at elevated temperature.
Approximately 5 at% W will improve the phase stability and melting point of TiVNbTa.
W addition will reduce the rate of TiVNbTa strength degradation at elevated temperatures.
W addition will improve thermal-property matching and reduce thermal-expansion mismatch with the W substrate.
Keeping the W content low is necessary to avoid excessive embrittlement.
At 1273 K, 5 at% W-doped TiVNbTa will have statistically significantly greater yield and compressive strengths than undoped TiVNbTa.
At 1273 K, W-doped TiVNbTa will retain ductility near 40% strain.
W-doped TiVNbTa will maintain effective heat transfer across the W/intermediate-layer/CuCrZr assembly.
The proposed improvement is expected to remain effective up to approximately 1273 K and at strains around 30–40%.
Higher W concentrations or operation outside the stated boundaries may cause phase instability or excessive brittleness.
Refractory multiprincipal-element alloys exhibit a difficult tradeoff between ductility, high-temperature properties, alloy chemistry, and thermodynamic stability.
The optimal W concentration and the strength–ductility tradeoff in W-doped TiVNbTa are not established.

contradictions.description: The initial-state description associates the 1273 K strengths with about 40% strain, whereas the baseline specifies those strengths at 30% strain and identifies approximately 40% as room-temperature strain-to-failure.
